issues.legal_issue: A person charged with one offence may be convicted without a separate charge of a different offence that could have been charged in the alternative on the facts.
material_facts: The accused was charged with attempting to murder the injured person but was convicted of causing grievous hurt with a dangerous weapon, although that offence was not separately charged.
The court held that, on the facts, the trial judge could have charged the accused alternatively with the two offences.
issues.conclusion: The conviction for the uncharged offence was proper under section 237 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 236 and 237 of the Criminal Procedure Code permit a conviction for a different offence, even without a charge for it, where the facts would have permitted that offence to be charged in the alternative. The court applied Begu v. King Emperor (1925) 52 I.A. 191, which upheld a conviction for an offence not charged where the evidence established an offence that could have been charged.

rule.if: criminal_trial and accused_charged_with_one_offence and evidence_establishes_another_offence and alternative_offence_could_have_been_charged

predicates.criminal_trial: The accused was tried in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.accused_charged_with_one_offence: The prosecution charged the accused with one offence.
predicates.evidence_establishes_another_offence: The evidence at trial established that the accused committed an offence different from the one charged.
predicates.alternative_offence_could_have_been_char: The facts permitted the different offence to be charged as an alternative to the charged offence.

issues.definition: When a criminal trial establishes an offence that could have been charged as an alternative to the offence charged, the accused may be convicted of that alternative offence without a separate charge.

issues.legal_issue: A failure to examine an accused fully does not require a conviction to be set aside unless the failure materially prejudiced the accused.
material_facts: After the prosecution evidence, the trial judge asked the accused three questions about the evidence, the dispute and the injuries, and whether the accused would call evidence.
The court considered the case uncomplicated, found the questioning adequate in the circumstances, and found no material showing that the accused was prejudiced.
issues.conclusion: The examination did not justify setting aside the conviction; an accused must show material prejudice from an inadequate examination.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code, it is not enough to show that the accused was not fully examined; the accused must also show that the examination materially prejudiced the defence.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and accused_questioning_was_limited and issues_were_simple and no_material_prejudice_was_shown

predicates.criminal_appeal: The matter is an appeal from a criminal conviction.
predicates.accused_questioning_was_limited: The trial judge asked the accused only a limited number of questions about the prosecution evidence and the defence.
predicates.issues_were_simple: The matters the accused needed to address were uncomplicated.
predicates.no_material_prejudice_was_shown: The accused did not show that the limited examination materially harmed the defence.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal, limited questioning on uncomplicated issues, without shown material harm to the defence, does not require the conviction to be set aside.

issues.legal_issue: The non-examination of persons not shown to have witnessed the occurrence and a judge's comments on an unsupported defence do not invalidate a jury conviction where the evidence is sufficient and the jury is properly cautioned.
material_facts: The defence complained that several people living near the scene and a person present during a search had not been called, but there was no evidence that they witnessed the occurrence.
The prosecution evidence, if believed, was sufficient to support the conviction.
The accused suggested in cross-examination that the injured person had assaulted the accused's wife, but offered no evidence supporting that account.
The trial judge expressed scepticism about the defence suggestion but told the jurors that they need not accept the judge's view and should decide the matter themselves.
issues.conclusion: These complaints had no merit and did not justify disturbing the conviction.
issues.legal_principle: The court found no basis to disturb the jury's verdict where the proposed witnesses were not shown to have seen the event, the prosecution evidence could support the conviction, and the judge adequately warned the jury not to be influenced by the judge's view of the defence. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.jury_criminal_trial: The accused was tried for a criminal offence by a jury.
predicates.proposed_witnesses_not_shown_to_have_see: The accused relied on the absence of witnesses, but no evidence showed that those people had seen the occurrence.
predicates.prosecution_evidence_sufficient_if_belie: The prosecution evidence, if accepted, was sufficient to support the conviction.
predicates.judge_cautioned_jury_not_to_follow_judge: The judge told the jurors they were not bound by the judge's view of the defence and should decide the matter themselves.

issues.definition: In a jury trial, complaints about uncalled witnesses and judicial comments do not require a conviction to be set aside when the witnesses were not shown to have seen the event, the evidence could support conviction, and the jury was cautioned to decide independently.
